title: Transformations: normalisation, binning and derived variables

videos.script: Cleaning fixes what is wrong. This lesson is about what comes next: making new columns out of the clean ones. {{next}} The hour an order was placed. The day of the week. How many items it had. Whether the buyer was a company. None of these is in the file. All of them are one line of code. {{derived}} Each one is a small decision, and each has a way to go wrong. {{risk}} Attach a customer's total to every one of their orders, then add it up, and revenue grows twenty times. {{grain}} Cut ages into bands, and a twenty-five-year-old lands in a different band depending on one argument. {{bands}} Scale spending between zero and one, and one clinic's Christmas orders squeeze three customers in four into the bottom five per cent. {{scale}} Take a logarithm, and the hundred and thirty-seven orders charged nothing become minus infinity. {{log}} So every derived column in this lesson comes with its name, its formula and the trap it was checked for. {{end}}
